title: Ancient Trees in Denmark: Cities to Explore
meta_description: Copenhagen's remarkable trees come with tape measurements, working names and a 10-metre hollow oak north of the city. Two cities mapped, 23 trees.
intro: Copenhagen's remarkable trees come with tape measurements, which is rarer than it should be. The Danish dendrological society has surveyed them one by one and filed them under working names: a beech in Frederiksberg Have is registered as Bøgen ved Bådfarten, the beech by the boat trip, which makes it the easiest tree in the city to find. A honey locust has been on record since a gardening magazine featured it in 1941. Assistens cemetery holds five of the sixteen mapped here, and the thickest tree inside its walls is a sycamore, the least exotic species in it. The oldest is Skovfogedegen, a hollow oak 11 km north of the city at the edge of the royal deer park, which three Danish sources date to around the year 1200. Twenty-three trees mapped so far, across Copenhagen and Aarhus.
